problem: The company had fallen short of privacy and security expectations.
title: Zoom freezes new features for 90 days to fix privacy and security
context: Zoom's usage surged in early 2020 and security and privacy problems came to light.
decision_made: Pause work on features not related to privacy, safety or security for 90 days.
action_taken: CEO Eric Yuan apologised, promised a third-party review, a transparency report and weekly webinars.
observed_outcome: Zoom published a follow-up on 1 July 2020 reporting on the 90-day programme. Coverage said the freeze was over but security stayed a priority; whether paused features returned was not established.
lessons: A public, time-boxed commitment to fix trust issues can be easier to hold the company to than a general promise.
limitations: The result is described mainly by the company's own report. Effects on user trust and growth were not measured in the sources used.

claims.claim_text: Zoom paused work on non-security and non-privacy features for 90 days.
Zoom published a CEO report on the 90 days on 1 July 2020.
